chapter: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
title: Big-Eye Louis, Picou and other New Orleans clarinetists
summary: Danny describes Big-Eye Louis Nelson and Picou as masters of improvised clarinet and he and Milt try to recall an island clarinetist.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Big-Eye Louis [Nelson] was a great clarinet player, who was somewhat of a rival of Tio. Big-Eye Louis and Picou, they were masters of that style of playing, that improvisation...
Was Jay-Joe(?) from here? A clarinet player named Jay-Joe(?).
No, I think he was from Cuba.
Oh, yeah. He came to Chicago.
Yeah, Jay-Joe(?) and the other one, the one who plays clarinet upside-down.
I can't think of his name. It wasn't Cliff Keene, was it?
No. It was another guy. Later Paul showed me him in New York. He was a master clarinet player from one of them islands.
